content: Never call `exit` (or `die`) in application code, including after `$response->send()`. Under a test runner it terminates the process mid-test with zero output — no test name, no failure, no summary — so the run looks like a crash with no cause, and the failure appears to belong to whatever file happened to be collected. Under a queue worker or console command it kills the process mid-job, and it skips terminable middleware and the rest of the response lifecycle. To return a response from deep in the stack, throw `HttpResponseException` instead: HTTP requests still get the response via the exception handler, and every other context gets an ordinary catchable exception. When a test file dies mute, suspect `exit` in the code under test before suspecting the test.
context: ISS-018. AsAuthenticatedTest exited 2 with zero bytes and took the whole App suite's reporting down. The filed diagnosis blamed an undefined `api` guard, which was a real but separate bug in a different test in the same file. The actual killer was `redirect()->route($route)->send(); exit;` in AuthenticatedDecorator::handleUnauthenticated(), on the non-JSON branch. Proved by printing a marker either side of a direct handle() call: the first marker printed, the redirect HTML dumped to stdout, the second never ran. Because the output is empty, nothing points at the responsible line — bisecting test by test and watching which one produces zero bytes was the only thing that found it. After replacing exit with HttpResponseException the App suite went from producing no summary at all to a full 53 failed / 8 skipped / 103 passed.
title: exit in application code kills the test runner with no output, and kills queue workers in production
